extracted.intended_audience: applicants, trademark attorneys, businesses, and Patent Office personnel dealing with trademark and appellation-of-origin registration and enforcement in the Russian Federation
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules governing definition, registration, examination, rights, use, transfer, renewal, cancellation, appeals, and enforcement for trademarks, collective marks, and appellations of origin in the Russian Federation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of trademark/service mark
rubrics_metrics.description: The trademark and the service mark are designations capable of distinguishing the goods and services of legal or natural persons from similar goods and services of other persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory definitional threshold for what constitutes a trademark for all subsequent rules (Articles 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for legal protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal protection of a trademark is accorded either on the basis of its state registration in accordance with this Law or by the operation of international treaties of the Russian Federation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right to a trademark is protected by law; a trademark may be registered in the name of a legal or natural person engaged in business (Article 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark certificate effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark certificate is issued for a registered trademark and establishes the priority date and the exclusive right of the trademark owner in respect of the goods specified in the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate evidences priority and exclusive scope limited to listed goods (Article 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights and infringement acts
rubrics_metrics.description: The trademark owner has the exclusive right to use and dispose of the trademark and to forbid its use by others; unauthorized manufacture, use, importation, offer for sale, sale, or other introduction into commerce of the trademark or a confusingly similar designation is infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement is defined by unauthorized acts 'to such a degree as to confuse' consumers; consent of owner required for lawful use (Article 4, Item 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible trademark types
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal, figurative, three-dimensional and other designations or combinations thereof may be registered as trademarks; trademarks may be registered in any colour or colour combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad statutory allowance for forms of marks (Article 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — lack of distinctiveness and other unregistrable signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks consisting merely of designations lacking distinctiveness; national coats of arms, flags and emblems; official names of states; names of international organizations; official signs, warranty/control seals, awards; designations that have entered the public domain as names of goods of a definite kind; generally accepted symbols and terms; indications of type, quality, quantity, properties, purpose, value of goods, venue and time of manufacture or sale shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some of these elements may be incorporated as non-protectable elements into a trademark unless they hold a dominant position (Article 6, Item 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — false, misleading or immoral marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Designations that are false or capable of causing consumer confusion regarding the product or its manufacturer, or that are contrary to public interest, humanitarian or moral principles, shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General public interest and consumer-protection as absolute bars (Article 6, Item 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — identity/similarity to prior rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Designations identical or similar to a degree of confusion to trademarks already registered or pending in the Russian Federation for similar goods, trademarks protected by international treaties, appellations of origin, or certification marks shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when earlier rights belong to another person; incorporation of some elements as non-protectable elements is allowed in limited cases (Article 7, Item 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds — use of protected company names, designs, works, portraits
rubrics_metrics.description: Designations reproducing company names known in the Russian Federation, industrial designs owned by others, titles/characters/quotations/works of art without consent, surnames/names/pseudonyms/portraits of renowned people without consent (or relevant authority/ heirs) shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes special protection for historical/cultural heritage designations and references to Rules for Recognizing a Trade Mark as Generally Known (Article 7, Item 2 and following paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing authority and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for registering a trademark must be filed by a legal or natural person with the State Patent Office (Patent Office) and may be filed through a patent agent/attorney registered with the Patent Office; foreign applicants must act through patent attorneys registered with the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority of patent attorneys must be evidenced by power of attorney; Patent Office sets attorney requirements (Article 8, Items 1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: One trademark per application and mandatory contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall relate to a single trademark and must contain a petition indicating the applicant and location, the designation as applied for and its description, and the list of goods grouped by classes per the International Classification of Goods and Services for the Registration of Marks; the application shall be submitted in Russian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attached documents (proof of payment, charter for collective mark) must be in Russian or translated; translations may be submitted within two months; Patent Office prescribes document requirements (Article 8, Items 3–6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority — filing date and Convention/Exhibition priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date is date of receipt by the Patent Office of an application meeting Article 8(4) requirements; convention priority may be claimed if first-filed in a Paris Convention country and received within six months; exhibition priority may be claimed if first publicly demonstrated at official exhibitions and received within six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enjoy convention/exhibition priority applicant must claim it when filing or within two months of receipt and enclose supporting documents (Article 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert examination — preliminary and substantive phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert examination by the Patent Office consists of a preliminary examination and an examination of the designation applied for; the applicant may supplement or amend application materials before a decision, but materials that change the application on its merits must be filed as a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office may request additional materials (two-month response time); failure to respond may lead to deemed withdrawal; applicant may withdraw any time before registration (Article 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary expert examination is carried out within one month of receipt and verifies the content of the application, presence and compliance of documents; result is acceptance for consideration or refusal of acceptance; acceptance triggers notice of established priority except where convention/exhibition priority documents are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of required documents crucial to establish filing date/priority (Article 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The expert examination of the designation considers compliance with Articles 1, 6 and Item 1 of Article 7 (definition, absolute and relative refusal grounds) and establishes filing date if not already done; decision to register or reject follows examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to register may be reconsidered if an earlier priority date is shown (Article 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals procedure and time-limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may appeal decisions to the Chamber of Appeals within three months of receipt; Chamber must consider appeals within four months; further appeal to the Supreme Patent Chamber within six months; decisions of Supreme Patent Chamber are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has right to access materials referenced in the decision and request copies within one month; missed time-limits may be reinstated within two months upon petition with valid reasons and payment (Article 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration recording and required particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: On decision to register, the Patent Office shall record the trademark in the State Register within one month of proof of payment; the Register records the trademark, owner information, priority and registration dates, list of goods, and related particulars and subsequent changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration entries are the authoritative public record (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue and form of trademark certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office shall issue the trademark certificate within three months of the registration date; layout and particulars of the certificate are determined by the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate formalities controlled administratively (Article 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of validity and renewal of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is valid for ten years from the date of receipt of the application by the Patent Office and may be renewed upon owner request submitted within the last year of validity, each time for ten years; a six‑month grace period may be granted with supplementary duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal recorded in Register and certificate; see rules for prolongation (Article 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to registration particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark owner must notify the Patent Office of any changes in company name, personal name, restriction of goods list, changes in certain trademark elements which do not affect essence, and other registration-related changes; such changes recorded upon payment of duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying and recording changes preserves the public record accuracy (Article 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information recorded in the Register shall be published by the Patent Office in the official bulletin within six months of registration or of changes being made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication ensures third-party notice (Article 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign and international registration processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons of the Russian Federation are entitled to register trademarks in foreign countries or internationally; applications for international registration shall be filed through the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office acts as intermediary for international filings (Article 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective mark definition and non-transferability
rubrics_metrics.description: A collective mark is the mark of an amalgamation (union, association) used to designate goods manufactured/sold by its members possessing unified qualitative or other common features; the collective mark and the right to use it are not transferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective marks linked to membership and quality standards (Article 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective mark registration requirements (charter content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for a collective mark must include a charter specifying the name of the amalgamation authorized to register, the list of enterprises entitled to use the mark, purpose of registration, list of unified qualitative/common features, conditions for use, monitoring procedure, and liability for charter violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register records enterprises entitled to use the mark and publishes an extract from the charter concerning unified features; owner must notify changes; misuse (use on goods lacking features) may lead to termination (Article 21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trademark — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing the trademark on goods or their packaging by the owner or licensed party is deemed use; use in advertising, publications, letterheads, billboards, or exhibits may count as use when valid reasons exist for non‑use on goods/packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediaries may use their trademark with or instead of manufacturer's; use evidence is relevant to non-use cancellation proceedings (Article 22, Items 1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-use and early termination for non-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration may be terminated (in whole or in part) for continuous non-use for five years from registration date or for five years preceding a request; owner's evidence of non-use for reasons beyond control may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-year non-use is statutory ground for cancellation; proof and valid reasons can rebut (Article 22, Item 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion/limits on rights from registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration does not empower owner to prohibit use of the trademark by others with respect to goods that have been put on the market directly by the trademark owner or with his consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition of exhaustion doctrine in respect of goods placed on market by owner/with consent (Article 23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning mark for trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark owner may use a warning mark with the trademark showing that the designation is a trademark registered in the Russian Federation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative device to indicate registered status (Article 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment (concession) of trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark may be assigned by its owner to a legal or natural person in relation to all or part of the goods for which it was registered; assignment is not permitted if it may cause consumer confusion regarding the product or its manufacturer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers limited to avoid confusion and protect consumers (Article 25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing quality control obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: License contract must stipulate that the licensee's quality of goods shall not be inferior to that of the licensor and that the licensor will monitor observance of this term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality control clause is mandatory to license the use of a trademark (Article 26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of assignment and license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts conceding a trademark and license contracts must be registered with the Patent Office; absence of such registration renders them invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration requirement makes assignment/license invalid if unrecorded (Article 27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for recognition of registration as invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration may be recognized invalid fully or in part during its term if effected in violation of Article 2(3) requirements or Article 6 (absolute grounds), or within five years of publication under grounds in Article 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person may file an objection; objection examined within four months; appeals follow Chamber and Supreme Patent Chamber timelines (Article 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation triggers for registered trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office shall cancel registration by reason of expiry, Supreme Patent Chamber decision (e.g., misuse of collective mark or non-use), recognition as invalid, liquidation of owner, transformation into a public-domain designation of goods of a definite kind, or express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated statutory grounds for administrative cancellation (Article 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of appellation of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellation of the origin of goods is the name of a country, locality or other geographic place used to designate goods whose specific features are exclusively or primarily determined by natural conditions or human factors characteristic of that geographic object; historical names may qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations that have entered public domain as names of goods not related to place do not qualify (Article 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for legal protection of appellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal protection of an appellation of origin results from its registration under this Law or by operation of international treaties; the appellation may be registered by one or more persons and the registrant receives the right to use it if goods meet Article 30 requirements; registration has no time-limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right to use may be conferred to persons located in same geographic object producing goods with same features (Article 31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements for appellations of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Application to register and grant the right to use an appellation must be filed with the Patent Office, relate to one appellation, contain a petition (applicant and location), the designation, product type and venue boundaries, and a description of the product's specific features; application in Russian; attachments include a document from competent authority confirming applicant's location and production and proof of payment; foreign applicants provide certification of rights in country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations allowed within two months; Patent Office sets document requirements (Article 32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert examination procedure for appellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert examination of appellation applications consists of a preliminary and substantive examination; applicant may supplement materials; additional materials requested must be furnished within two months; preliminary examination within two months checks contents and documents; substantive examination checks compliance with Article 30; decisions may register, refuse, grant right to use already registered appellation, or refuse; applicant may withdraw any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-limits and supplementation rules parallel trademark procedure (Article 33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and reinstatement for appellation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may appeal preliminary/substantive examination decisions to the Chamber of Appeals within three months; Chamber considers within four months; further appeal to Supreme Patent Chamber within six months; missed terms may be reinstated by Patent Office within two months on petition showing valid reasons and payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors trademark appeals structure (Article 34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and certificate for appellation use
rubrics_metrics.description: On decision to register and grant right to use, Patent Office records the appellation in the State Register of Appellations and issues a certificate for use within three months of proof of payment; the Register contains the appellation, certificate owner information, product type, description of specific features, and subsequent changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form and particulars of the certificate determined by the Patent Office (Article 35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and renewal of appellation certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate is valid for ten years from receipt of the application and may be renewed upon request during the last year of validity together with a document from a competent authority confirming location and production; renewal each time for ten years; six-month grace term with additional duty possible; renewal recorded in Register and certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural parallels to trademark renewal; rules for prolongation are referenced (Article 36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and publication for appellation registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate owner shall notify Patent Office of changes in company/person name or other registration-related changes which shall be recorded upon payment; information about registration and granting of right to use shall be published in official bulletin within six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains public record and transparency (Articles 37–38).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign registration of appellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and natural persons may register appellations of origin in foreign countries; applications for foreign registration should be filed after domestic registration and grant of right to use in the Russian Federation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective sequence: domestic registration first (Article 39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use restrictions for appellations — unauthorized use and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing the appellation on product, packaging, advertisements, prospectuses, bills, letterheads, and related documents is deemed use; use of a registered appellation by persons without a certificate is not permitted even if true origin is indicated or used in translated form or with words like 'kind', 'type', 'imitation'; use of a similar designation for similar goods capable of causing consumer confusion as to origin/features is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate owner is not authorized to grant licenses for use of the appellation (Article 40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning mark for appellations
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate owner may use a warning mark with the appellation showing that the designation is a registered appellation of origin in the Russian Federation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent feature to trademark warning mark (Article 41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation and termination grounds for appellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration may be recognized void if effected in violation of the Law; registration may be terminated if conditions characteristic to the geographic place disappear making manufacture impossible; foreign registrant may lose registration if they lose the right in country of origin; certificate may be void if granted in violation; certificate validity may be terminated for loss of recorded properties, cancellation of appellation registration, liquidation of owner, or at owner's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections may be filed and appealed; Patent Office cancels registration/certificates if Supreme Patent Chamber finds them invalid (Article 42).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Patent Office functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Patent Office shall carry out uniform policy protecting trademarks and appellations, accept and examine applications, effect registrations, issue certificates, publish official information, print rules/clarifications, and perform other functions related to trademarks and appellations of origin in accordance with its statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central administrative authority for implementation and registration (Article 43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official duties and administration fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Official duties shall be collected for legally significant acts related to registration of trademarks and registration/granting of rights to use appellations of origin; duties payable to the Patent Office; Government establishes list of actions, amounts, payment terms and grounds for return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative fee structure governed by Government regulation (Article 44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution fora
rubrics_metrics.description: Disputes arising from the application of this Law are resolved according to Russian legislation by courts, arbitration courts, or mediation boards; includes disputes over infringement, license/assignment contracts, and illegal use of appellations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supreme Patent Chamber examines disputes within its authority under specified Articles (Article 45).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability and remedies for illegal use of trademarks/appellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal use of trademarks or appellations (or confusingly similar designations) entails civil and/or criminal liability; remedies include claims to stop infringement, compensation for damage, publication of judicial decisions to restore reputation, elimination or destruction of illegally used trademarks/designations/samples; for appellations additionally require cessation, compensation, payment to local authority of profits obtained in excess of compensated losses, publication, elimination/destruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of warning mark for unregistered marks is also liable under law; multiple civil and criminal enforcement tools available (Article 46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of foreign persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign legal and natural persons enjoy rights under this Law on equal level with Russian persons by virtue of international treaties or reciprocity; right to register appellations of origin is granted to persons of countries that grant similar rights to Russian persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-discrimination subject to treaties and reciprocity (Article 47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supremacy of international treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: If international treaties of the Russian Federation establish rules different from this Law, the rules of the international treaties shall apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International obligations take precedence where they differ (Article 48).
